sections.html:
The Register of Deeds works from 375 Church Street, Suite 106, Dayton, TN 37321, and the number to call is 423-775-7841.

Tennessee files land records county by county. Any Rhea County house, from a bungalow in Dayton to acreage outside Spring City or Graysville, is recorded at this single window. A quick phone call saves a wasted drive: confirm the fee schedule now in force, the office hours for your visit day, and whether clerks insist on the wet-ink original or take something else.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Rhea County?
sections.html:
What the register charges per page is set locally, so ring 423-775-7841 for today's number. Tax is a different matter. The state fixes it, and it is usually the bigger piece of what you hand over at the counter.

Tennessee recordation taxes collected at the register
State recordation chargeRate
Realty transfer tax on a deed$0.37 per $100
Mortgage (indebtedness) tax on a deed of trust$0.115 per $100, first $2,000 exempt

The page fee for the register's own work is added to each total.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Rhea County home sale
sections.html:
Every real estate transfer owes $0.37 per $100 under Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409. The Revenue Department's help desk says the base is generally whichever is larger, the price paid or the property's value.

Because the larger number wins, writing a token price on the deed for a house worth far more does nothing to lower the bill. Anyone planning a family transfer or a below-market sale should raise the figure with the title agent before signing. When the buyer borrows, the recording of the deed of trust brings a second levy, $0.115 per $100 of debt past the first $2,000.

Your contract allocates each line between buyer and seller, so study the settlement statement before closing day. Should the counter total disagree with the estimate you were given, staff will explain how they reached it.

sections.h2: Which Rhea County offices handle the rest of a sale?
sections.html:
Recording is one stop of three, and the others are under the same roof at 375 Church Street in Dayton.

  • Rhea County Property Assessor, Suite 100, 423-775-7840: parcel values and ownership maps
  • Rhea County Trustee, Suite 110, 423-775-7810: property tax bills and payoff amounts
  • Rhea County Register of Deeds, Suite 106, 423-775-7841: recording of the deed and mortgage

Sequence counts. The Trustee supplies a payoff first, the title company receives it, and only then does the deed go to the register. Find out from the Trustee which year is open and whether penalties or older delinquencies hang on it, since any back tax is taken out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: Questions to ask the register before you close
sections.html:
Bring these to the staff at 423-775-7841 and you will likely avoid a return visit.

  • What is the total recording fee for a deed of my page count?
  • Does the deed need any reference to a prior book and page?
  • Has the office received the release for the mortgage being paid off?
  • How will the recorded original be returned, and how long does it take?
  • Can a title company record by an electronic method, or does it need to deliver the paper?

Fees and forms shift over time, so treat each answer as good for the day you asked. In an as-is cash sale the deed is normally the lone filing, which makes for a brisk visit once everything is signed.

sections.h2: How a Rhea County sale moves from contract to recorded deed
sections.html:
Most of the work happens away from the courthouse. A seller can expect roughly this path.

  1. Sign the contract, which assigns the transfer tax and recording fees to one side or the other.
  2. Ask the title company to confirm who actually holds title, because a deed sitting in a relative's name must be sorted out before any buyer can close.
  3. Gather the Trustee's tax payoff along with a release from each lender being paid off.
  4. Sign the deed in front of a notary and let the title company carry it over for filing.
  5. Keep a copy of the recorded deed with your closing papers.

Anyone who inherited the property should take the recorded chain of deeds to an attorney or title company before listing. Gaps in that chain are what most often hold a sale up.

sections.h2: What to bring when you visit the Dayton office
sections.html:
A clerk can file only what lands on the counter, and a thin packet means driving back across the county. Phone first, then show up with the full set.

  • The signed and notarized deed, as an original unless staff say another format works.
  • Payment for the state tax and the register's per-page fee, in whatever form staff tell you they accept.
  • The names of the parties spelled exactly as they appear on the prior deed.
  • The book and page of the previous recording, if your title agent has it.
  • A phone number where the office can reach you if something is missing.

Mismatched name spellings are a quiet source of delay. A deed that calls the seller one thing when the chain of title calls the seller another can send the title company back to fix it. Reading the earlier deed against your own ahead of time takes a few minutes and prevents most of that.

sections.h2: Why recording order matters for a seller
sections.html:
Filing is the act that makes a sale public. Until it happens, nobody searching the books can see the buyer's ownership, and the Assessor has no reason to change the parcel. The gap between signing and filing is usually short, though you should still ask the title company when it will occur.

Paying off a mortgage runs the other direction. Once the loan is satisfied the lender releases its lien, and the release is filed so title reads clean. If it has not reached the register by closing, the title company can keep part of your proceeds in reserve. A call asking whether the release has arrived heads that off.

As of July 1, 2025 the county is estimated at 34,844 residents, a gain of 4.8 percent over the April 2020 base. Housing totals 15,955 units across 13,475 households, with 71.5 percent of occupied homes lived in by their owners. The median owner-occupied value is $206,000 for 2020 to 2024. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,326, and owners without one report $365. Median gross rent is $839. Dayton is the county seat and largest town, with Graysville and Spring City as the other towns.

faqs.q: Where is a Rhea County deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Rhea County Register of Deeds, 375 Church Street, Suite 106, Dayton, TN 37321. The phone number is 423-775-7841.

faqs.q: How much is the Tennessee transfer tax on a Rhea County sale?
faqs.a: It is $0.37 per $100, generally on the greater of the price paid or the property's value. The register's own recording fee is added on top.

faqs.q: Is there a mortgage tax in Rhea County?
faqs.a: Yes, a state indebtedness tax of $0.115 per $100 applies to the loan when its deed of trust is recorded, with the first $2,000 left out.

faqs.q: Who gets my property tax payoff in Rhea County?
faqs.a: The Rhea County Trustee, 375 Church Street, Suite 110, at 423-775-7810. Ask for the open balance and any interest to your closing date, and give it to the title company.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Rhea County house if the deed is still in a parent's name?
faqs.a: A title agent has to resolve who holds title before a buyer can close. Ask the register at 423-775-7841 what the recorded chain of deeds shows, and bring the findings to an attorney or title company.
